# BTicino C300X Native Agent Integration v0.4.0

Feature release focused on native WebRTC talkback preparation, SIP/Flexisip
configuration, and codec/legal clarity.

## Highlights

- Native C media bridge SIP/Flexisip endpoint settings are configurable instead
  of being hardcoded.
- Doorbell WebRTC audio now tracks one-way door-station audio separately from
  browser microphone talkback.
- Talkback diagnostics expose whether HTTPS is required, whether talkback was
  requested, whether it is active, sent packet count, and the last local error.
- Optional local Home Assistant frontend HTTPS helper supports browser
  microphone tests; the native C300X agent itself remains HTTP-only on the
  local LAN.
- Legal notes clarify that the project does not ship codec binaries or codec
  implementation code; H.264/AVC is the device-provided stream and Speex is used
  for talkback RTP.

## Security and Privacy

- No token values, broker passwords, callback URLs, firmware payloads, APKs,
  copied stock QML pages, codec binaries, or third-party controller code are
  included.
- Talkback remains bound to an active Home Assistant WebRTC camera session and
  does not add idle device traffic.
- Browser microphone access requires an HTTPS Home Assistant frontend origin.

## Notes

- The C300X must already be rooted or SSH-enabled before the native agent can be
  installed.
- Two-way audio depends on browser microphone support and HTTPS. Local HTTP
  Home Assistant frontends can still display video but cannot provide a browser
  microphone track.
